ops.text: Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data. As between the Parties, Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Properties and all other data and information provided by or collected from Customer or the Properties (collectively, "Customer Data"), together with all deliverables and work product created for Customer under this Agreement, and Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to such deliverables and work product. Kubient retains all right, title and interest in its pre-existing intellectual property and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any Kubient intellectual property embedded in such deliverables. No deliverable, work product or Customer Data shall be jointly owned.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no ownership clause, so we add one short sentence pair confirming we own the deliverables and work product created for us (with Kubient assigning them) and retain all rights in our Content, Properties and Customer Data, while Kubient keeps its pre-existing IP and licenses to us, on a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free basis, any Kubient intellectual property embedded in the deliverables, with no joint ownership. This is our preferred IP position; if helpful, we can instead work from the fallback under which Kubient owns its generic tools and know-how and we take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to the deliverables.
proposal.summary: Insert a concise ownership clause: AP owns deliverables and work product (Kubient assigns) and retains all rights in Customer Data; Kubient keeps pre-existing IP and grants a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Kubient IP embedded in deliverables; no joint ownership.
